stories.title_en: Talking a Sister-in-Law into Adultery to Cheat Oil and Meat

paragraphs.zh: 两妯娌并坐，适有卖油者过。婶石氏曰：“家下要油用，奈无银可买。”姆左氏曰：“先秤油来，约后还银未迟。”石氏叫入买油，秤定二斤矣。曰：“男人未在家，过两日来接银。”后两日卖油者来，婶曰：“无银，何以处？”姆曰：“再约三日。”婶以此言退之去。又三日，婶曰：“你教我先秤油，今竟无银。你讨些借我还。”姆曰：“你肯依我教，还他何难？”婶曰：“我凡事常依你，把甚物还？”姆曰：“我看卖油后生俊俏，你青年貌美，和他相好一次，油何消还？”婶曰：“恐你后日说。”姆曰：“是我教你，怎敢说？我避在房中，你自去为之。”
paragraphs.en: Two sisters-in-law were sitting together when an oil seller passed. The younger, Shi, said: “We need oil at home, but have no silver to buy it.” The elder, Zuo, said: “Have him weigh the oil first; paying later is soon enough.” Shi called him in and bought two jin. She said: “The men aren’t home; come in two days for the silver.” Two days later the oil seller came. The younger said: “No silver; what to do?” The elder said: “Set another three days.” The younger used this to send him away. After three more days, the younger said: “You told me to weigh the oil first; now there’s no silver. Lend me some to pay him.” The elder said: “If you’ll do as I teach, paying him is easy.” The younger said: “I always do as you say; what should I use to pay?” The elder said: “I see that oil-seller lad is handsome, and you’re young and pretty; have a fling with him once—why pay for the oil?” The younger said: “I’m afraid you’ll talk later.” The elder said: “I taught you; how would I dare talk? I’ll hide in the room; you go do it.”

paragraphs.zh: 少顷，卖油者到。石氏思无计可退，强作笑脸，出迎曰：“两次约你接银，奈何无可措办，不如把我还你罢。”卖油者见其眉开眼笑，亦起淫心曰：“你家内有人，莫非哄我？”石氏曰：“丈夫去耕田，伯姆在邻家绩麻。因无人，故与你耍言。”卖油者放心，与入房去。左氏听已拴房门，即密出，将两半篓油倾起，把两半篓水注入，再到房门密听。婶曰：“完了，起去。”卖油者曰：“与我停停。”左氏手持麻筐，跳身出大门外，故扬言曰：“今日尚未午，何耕田的回了？”卖油者闻人言，忙出挑油，恰相遇于门外。左氏问曰：“婶婶油还你否？”卖油者连应曰：“还了！还了！”即挑过一村卖。左氏知其必再来，站在大门候。
paragraphs.en: Shortly the oil seller arrived. Shi had no way to put him off, forced a smile, came out, and said: “Twice I set a date to pay; I can’t raise the money. Better pay you with myself.” The oil seller saw her smiling, and lust rose: “There are people in your house; are you tricking me?” Shi said: “Husband’s in the fields; sister-in-law is next door spinning hemp. There’s no one, so I’m teasing you.” The oil seller was reassured and went into the room. Zuo heard the door bolted, slipped out, poured out both half-baskets of oil, poured water into both, then went back to listen at the door. The younger said: “Done, get up.” The oil seller said: “Wait a bit with me.” Zuo, hemp basket in hand, jumped out the main gate and deliberately called: “It’s not even noon; how is the field-worker back?” The oil seller heard, hurriedly came out with his oil, and met her at the gate. Zuo asked: “Did Aunt pay you for the oil?” The oil seller quickly said: “Paid! Paid!” and carried it to the next village to sell. Zuo knew he would come back, and waited at the main gate.

paragraphs.zh: 近午，卖油者向前。左氏曰：“你尚在此？我婶婶的弟挑桶来打涝，见油一担在宅，家并无人，只婶房有人笑话，疑与卖油人有奸，将油倾在桶去，把半篓水注满，归报其母，母子径来拿奸。及来时，挑油的已去，正在此猜疑。叵知你在此，必拿你作对。”卖油者便行。左氏扯住曰：“我报你知，你须谢我。”卖油者曰：“明日寄两斤油与你。”
paragraphs.en: Near noon the oil seller came forward. Zuo said: “You’re still here? Aunt’s brother came with buckets to fetch water, saw a load of oil in the house, no one around, only laughing in Aunt’s room, suspected adultery with the oil seller, poured the oil into his buckets, filled the half-baskets with water, went home and told his mother; mother and son came to catch them. By the time they arrived, the oil carrier was gone; they’re still guessing here. If they knew you were here they’d surely take you as the culprit.” The oil seller started to go. Zuo grabbed him: “I tipped you off; you should thank me.” The oil seller said: “Tomorrow I’ll send you two jin of oil.”

paragraphs.zh: 过数日，果寄油来。姆又变说，持与婶曰：“前日我在门站，卖油者复从门前过。我故耍之曰：‘婶婶说油银未还，你适间慌忙说还了，必有缘故。我在此等报叔叔。’卖油者心虚，许我两斤油，今果寄来。此是你换来的，须当补你。”婶曰：“似此半时光景，也是四斤油用，多谢指教。”姆曰：“你若依我，更有别享用处。”
paragraphs.en: After several days, he did send oil. The elder changed the story, took it to the younger, and said: “The other day I was standing at the gate; the oil seller passed again. I teased him: ‘Aunt says the oil silver isn’t paid; you hurriedly said it was paid—there must be a reason. I’m waiting here to tell Uncle.’ He felt guilty, promised me two jin; now he’s sent it. This is what you swapped for; I should make it up to you.” The younger said: “In that half hour I got four jin of oil to use; thanks for the teaching.” The elder said: “If you listen to me, there are more good things to enjoy.”

paragraphs.zh: 少顷，有人叫卖肉。姆婶二人叫入，各秤二斤，吩咐再来接银。三日，屠子来接。伯姆秤银七分还之，婶的再约两日。至期，屠子来。伯姆曰：“你依前日套子还他，我方便入房内去。”石氏出，笑对屠子曰：“借你肉，无银可还。今日无人在家，不如把我肉还你。”屠子见其美貌，嬉嬉笑曰：“我只要你腰间些些肉。”石氏曰：“全身都允你，何惜些些？”屠子搂抱入房干事。伯姆潜出，把一担肉都搬入讫，默坐在肉箩边。
paragraphs.en: Soon someone called selling meat. The two called him in, each weighed two jin, and told him to come back for silver. In three days the butcher came. The elder weighed seven fen of silver to pay; the younger’s was set for two more days. When the time came, the butcher arrived. The elder said: “Do the same trick as before to pay him; I’ll conveniently go into the room.” Shi came out, smiled at the butcher, and said: “I borrowed your meat, no silver to pay. Today no one’s home; better pay you with my meat.” The butcher saw her looks, grinned, and said: “I only want a little meat around your waist.” Shi said: “The whole body is yours; why begrudge a little?” The butcher embraced her into the room. The elder slipped out, moved the whole load of meat inside, and sat silently by the meat baskets.

paragraphs.zh: 屠子与石氏欢罢而出，问曰：“我肉在哪里去？”左氏曰：“叔叔挑与里老去了。”屠子曰：“何得偷我肉？”左氏曰：“你好大胆！叔叔归，见肉担在此，入房门来又闭住，只闻你两人嘻嘻笑话，知是你奸他妻，叫我看住房门。我不好听你动静，故坐在此。你且略坐，停会偷肉的便来了。”屠子挑起空箩便走。左氏扯住曰：“把一肉刀与我做当头。”屠子曰：“托你方便，明日送两斤肉与你。”左氏放手，屠子飞步奔去。
paragraphs.en: The butcher finished with Shi and came out: “Where’s my meat?” Zuo said: “Uncle carried it to the village elder.” The butcher said: “How can you steal my meat?” Zuo said: “You’ve got nerve! Uncle came home, saw the meat load here, the bedroom door shut, heard you two laughing, knew you were with his wife, and told me to watch the door. I didn’t like listening to you, so I sat here. Sit a bit; the meat thief will be back soon.” The butcher picked up the empty baskets and ran. Zuo grabbed him: “Give me a meat knife as pledge.” The butcher said: “Thanks for the help; tomorrow I’ll send you two jin of meat.” Zuo let go; the butcher fled at a run.

paragraphs.zh: 婶埋怨曰：“都是你教我干此事。今丈夫知道，怎么是好？”姆曰：“你不该把师父摊出来。只要你肯食肉，此事何难遮盖？”婶曰：“有甚计策，快说出来。”姆入房，拖一腿肉出，又入拖一腿，曰：“你食肉乎？你报丈夫乎？”婶曰：“你偷肉，不该惊死我。”姆曰：“我惊那人；不惊他去，怎得他肉？”
paragraphs.en: The younger complained: “It was you who taught me to do this. Now husband knows—what then?” The elder said: “You shouldn’t have laid your teacher out in the open. If you’ll just eat the meat, this is easy to cover.” The younger said: “What’s the plan? Quick, say it.” The elder went in, dragged out one leg of meat, then another: “Will you eat the meat, or tell your husband?” The younger said: “You stole the meat; you shouldn’t have scared me to death.” The elder said: “I scared him; if I didn’t scare him off, how would we get his meat?”

paragraphs.zh: 两妯娌将肉煮来，把酒对吃。婶曰：“真是一日不识羞，三日吃饱饭。”姆曰：“不是如此说，是半时得快活，一月吃酒肉。”二人呵呵，饱吃一顿，餘者烟干后食。
paragraphs.en: The two cooked the meat and drank wine facing each other. The younger said: “Truly, one day of shamelessness, three days of full meals.” The elder said: “Not like that—half an hour of pleasure, a month of wine and meat.” They laughed, ate a full meal, and smoked the rest for later.

paragraphs.zh: 后数日，屠子经过，左氏出，支肉二斤，屠子速行。左氏曰：“亏我婶娘前日被一餐粗打，也该送二斤与她。”屠子将一片丢来，曰：“托你转上，我不得暇。”左氏手提两吊肉，入对婶娘说知，又将来作乐。婶曰：“我会养汉，不如你会光棍。”以后奸门一开，不可胜记。
paragraphs.en: A few days later the butcher passed. Zuo came out and took two jin of meat; the butcher hurried on. Zuo said: “Thanks to my aunt who took a beating the other day; you should send her two jin too.” The butcher tossed a piece: “Please put in a word; I haven’t time.” Zuo carried two strings of meat in, told the younger, and they made merry again. The younger said: “I can keep a lover; I’m not as good as you at being a swindler.” After that, once the adultery door was open, more than can be recorded.

paragraphs.zh: 按：石婶不过呆妇人，左姆乃狡猾巧妇；若是男子，当为大棍。遇此巧妇，愚者何不落其圈套？故不唯男子当择交，妇人尤当与良女相伴也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Aunt Shi was just a dull woman; Elder Zuo was a cunning, clever woman; if she were a man she would be a master swindler. Meeting such a clever woman, how would a fool not fall into her trap? So not only should men choose their company; women especially should keep company with good women.

stories.title_en: Incest with a Daughter-in-Law, Then Tricking Her Mother

paragraphs.zh: 乡间有一殷实村老，谷豆满仓，鸡鸭成群。只极是村恶，不知礼体。娶一田家女为媳妇，年少貌美，便思爬灰。只怕老妈严厉约束，家法整肃，积年不敢发。
paragraphs.en: In the countryside there was a well-off village elder, granaries full of grain and beans, chickens and ducks in flocks. He was extremely rustic and coarse, with no sense of rites. He married a farm girl as daughter-in-law, young and pretty, and thought of sleeping with her. He only feared the old lady’s strict control; household rules were tight; for years he dared not act.

paragraphs.zh: 一日，老妈邻家请饮，村老便调戏其妇。拒不从，遂行强抱。其妇喊起骂出，去外家只十里，便徒步奔告于母。母系村妇，惫赖愤怒，同女来。这村老见媳妇奔告外家，忙叫老妈回，以实情吐告，商量何以抵对。老妈心忖：“亲家村鲁，必不来，惟姻母惫赖必来。”已思有计笼之，故反言要老公曰：“恭喜你，喜事到矣！”村老曰：“往事已错，何须再题。你往日常能干，我凡事皆听你。今须救我，忽致破家。”老妈曰：“何止破家，你该死矣！我今救你来，你越胆大。若听我言，事过再勿起此野意，不但救你，且有好事抬举你。”村老曰：“不愿抬举，只救得这一遭，再不敢起恶意。若再有此，天诛地灭！”老妈曰：“既肯誓过，饶你这遭。你取银四两，作二锭，伏在外客房中，覆大下。若姻母来，我叫她在房来洗澡。你听其洗完，从下出，以两锭银付她两手。她必定拿住，推拒你不得，你便强奸一次。走出外去，事便息矣。”村老曰：“若奸她，则挑她女是真矣。”老妈曰：“你勿管，后事在我身。”村老依言，藏入大去。
paragraphs.en: One day the old lady was invited next door to drink. The village elder teased the daughter-in-law. She refused; he forced an embrace. She shouted and cursed her way out. Her natal home was only ten li away; she ran on foot to tell her mother. The mother was a village woman, vicious and furious, and came with her daughter. The village elder, seeing the daughter-in-law had run to tell her natal family, hurriedly called the old lady back, told the truth, and asked how to answer. The old lady thought: “The girl’s father is rustic; he won’t come. Only the girl’s mother, who’s vicious, will surely come.” She already had a plan to trap her, so she turned and congratulated her husband: “Congratulations! A happy event is here!” The village elder said: “What’s done is wrong; don’t bring it up again. You’ve always been capable; I listen to you in everything. Save me now; don’t let the family be ruined.” The old lady said: “Not only ruin—you’ll die! I save you now and you get bolder. If you listen to me, after this never raise this wild idea again; I’ll not only save you but have a happy affair to promote you.” The village elder said: “I don’t want promoting; just save me this once; I won’t dare raise a bad thought again. If I do, may Heaven strike me!” The old lady said: “Since you’ll swear, I’ll spare you this once. Get four taels of silver, make two ingots, hide in the outer guest room, under the big tub. When the girl’s mother comes, I’ll tell her to bathe in that room. After she’s done washing, you come out from under, put the two ingots in her two hands. She’ll certainly grab them and can’t push you off; then you force her once. Walk out, and the matter will rest.” The village elder said: “If I do her, then teasing her daughter is proven true.” The old lady said: “Don’t worry; the rest is on me.” He followed, and hid under the tub.

paragraphs.zh: 少顷，姻母到。老妈出外笑迎曰：“有劳贵步，未曾备轿迎得。”姻母便骂曰：“你家没伦理爬灰老贼，奸我女儿！”老妈故惊曰：“恰才哄我说，媳妇私煮炒吃，被他打骂，因逃归，乃有此恶事？我要和这老狗死！”大声大口，骂恨更切，姻母无待开口矣。因曰：“停会我、你、儿、媳四人，揪住打死，以大粪灌其口，使不为人。”即令媳妇把大鸡鸭宰，设盛馔待姻母。先大骂一场，后待茶果讫，曰：“走路身热，可讨水与洗澡，再好食午。”送姻母入房中洗，老妈入后厨房助妇整酒。及洗讫，下一人出，以银两锭付姻母，两手抱住便奸。及喊叫女儿、亲母，并无人应。其人曰：“她在厨房远，怎叫得知？”赤身难拒，又爱惜两槽银，哑口受奸。事讫，村老曰：“我就是亲家，你勿信女儿说。这成奸也是前缘，我本躲避你，谁知你送来洗澡，反先与你相好，从今再不望你女儿矣。”言罢走出。
paragraphs.en: Soon the girl’s mother arrived. The old lady came out smiling: “Sorry to trouble your honored steps; we didn’t prepare a sedan to meet you.” The mother cursed: “Your household has no ethics, you old thief who sleeps with his daughter-in-law—you raped my daughter!” The old lady pretended shock: “Just now he fooled me, said the daughter-in-law privately cooked a stir-fry, he beat and cursed her, so she fled home—there’s this evil thing? I’ll die with this old dog!” She cursed loudly and bitterly, even more fiercely, so the mother had no need to speak. Then: “In a bit, you, I, son, and daughter-in-law, the four of us, will grab him and beat him to death, pour nightsoil in his mouth, so he’s not fit to be a person.” She had the daughter-in-law kill big chickens and ducks and set a rich meal for the mother. First a round of loud cursing, then tea and fruit, then: “Walking makes you hot; fetch water for a bath, then we’ll eat the noon meal better.” She sent the mother into the room to wash; the old lady went to the back kitchen to help the daughter-in-law prepare wine. After washing, a man came out from under, put two ingots in the mother’s hands, held her, and forced her. She shouted for daughter and the old lady; no one answered. He said: “They’re in the kitchen far off; how would they hear?” Naked, hard to resist, and she coveted the two ingots of silver; she silently endured it. When done, the village elder said: “I’m the in-law; don’t believe your daughter’s talk. This affair was also predestined. I was hiding from you; who knew you’d be sent to bathe, and we’d get along first. From now on I won’t look to your daughter again.” Then he walked out.

paragraphs.zh: 姻母入厨，见女与老妈方在排馔，想叫时必是不闻，遂午间从容笑饮，不说及爬灰事矣。
paragraphs.en: The mother went to the kitchen, saw daughter and old lady still arranging dishes, thought they must not have heard her shouts, so at noon she drank and smiled at ease, and did not mention the incest.

paragraphs.zh: 席罢辞归，老妈再三苦留，女亦曰：“我叫你来做身主，你只要人酒吃，何这等老懵？”姻母曰：“我妇人自身不能作主，怎能做得你主？你公公不是好人，你妈妈贤德。只姑媳不相离，自无恶事矣。”老妈留之不得，以食品果仪厚赠之，欢喜送别而去。凄风骤雨之景色，倏化为光风化日之风景，皆能妇调停之力，———亦一大棍也。
paragraphs.en: After the meal she took leave. The old lady repeatedly urged her to stay; the daughter also said: “I called you to stand up for me; you only want people’s wine to drink—how can you be so old and muddled?” The mother said: “I as a woman can’t even stand up for myself; how can I stand up for you? Your father-in-law isn’t a good man; your mother-in-law is virtuous. If mother-in-law and daughter-in-law don’t part, there will be no more evil.” The old lady couldn’t keep her, gave generous food and fruit gifts, and happily saw her off. The scene of a bitter wind and sudden rain suddenly became bright breeze and fair sun—all by this capable woman’s mediating power. She too was a great swindler.

paragraphs.zh: 按：妇人不可轻易往外亲之家。若彼狡妇与昵夫套合，中多有被其污秽者，谁则知之？若此村老妇之弄姻母，虽一时解纷之巧计，亦彼自知妇人性皆流水，可以利暗诱奸暗陷，必不敢张胆明言也。后人其鉴之。
paragraphs.en: Note: Women should not go lightly to relatives’ homes. If a cunning woman and her intimate husband set a trap, many are defiled in it—who would know? As with this village old woman tricking the in-law mother: though it was a clever one-time way to settle a quarrel, she also knew that women’s nature is all like flowing water; they can be secretly lured with profit into a trap of illicit sex, and will never dare speak of it openly. Later people, take warning.

stories.title_en: A Tenant’s Wife Sells Sex to Strip the Landlord of Land

paragraphs.zh: 乡间有一佃户，欠主人苗三冬，算该本息银五两零。冬间，主人来收租，佃母与子谋曰：“苗带今年共欠三冬，明年必起田去，一家无望矣。我看主人富家子弟，必好风月，不如把媳妇哄他奸，拿住必可赖得苗去。”佃曰：“这事可。母亲可与媳妇言。”佃母曰：“还有一件，须要与他奸完了，然后拿住，他方甘心；若未成奸便拿，他是主人，怎肯受屈？又难赚他银矣。”佃曰：“亦可。”佃母方与媳妇言。妇曰：“你子心下实何如？”佃母曰：“我与儿说过了。任你事完成，然后拿他，方抵得苗去。”三人商议已定。
paragraphs.en: In the countryside there was a tenant who owed the landlord three winters of seedling-rent, calculated as over five taels principal and interest. In winter the landlord came to collect. The tenant’s mother plotted with her son: “With this year’s, we owe three winters of seedlings; next year he’ll surely take the land back; the whole family will have no hope. I see the landlord is a rich family’s son, must like romance; better have the daughter-in-law lure him into sex, catch him, and we can write off the rent.” The tenant said: “That can work. Mother, speak to the daughter-in-law.” The mother said: “One more thing: he must finish the act, then we catch him, so he’ll submit; if we catch before it’s done, he’s the landlord—why would he accept being wronged? And it’ll be hard to cheat him of silver.” The tenant said: “Also fine.” The mother then spoke to the daughter-in-law. The wife said: “What’s your son’s true mind?” The mother said: “I’ve spoken with my son. Let you finish the business, then catch him, so it can offset the rent.” The three agreed.

paragraphs.zh: 次日饭后，佃推往岳丈家借银来还苗。佃母又吩咐媳妇曰：“主人来无菜，我往上村讨斤肉，再往叔家取个鸡来。苗有还否，须做一东道与主人吃。你须备火炉与主人向。”主人在外已闻。二人去后，妇拾火炉出煽火。主人问曰：“你妈妈哪里去？”妇曰：“去讨菜。”又问曰：“你丈夫何去？”妇曰：“到我娘家去借银还你苗，未知有否？”主人曰：“不消问你娘借，只消问你借。”妇曰：“我若有银，早送来还了。”主曰：“昨夜早同我睡，便与你对苗去。”妇曰：“睡可当得银，今夜来陪你。”主人便起曰：“不待夜间，今日喜得无人，就耍去。你夫借得银来，我背地秤三钱与你买布；若无银，且宽限你明年还。”妇人即允，同入房去。佃户从密处窥见，悄悄出候房门外。只听房内二人欢话，心中自然焦燥，恨不得即打进去。半晌久，主人曰：“起去罢。”妇曰：“从容无妨。”知其完了，在房外高声喝曰：“你和甚人讲话？”打入门去。二人忙不能躲。佃户喝曰：“嗳也！你这贼奸我妻！”便在床上揪下打。妻忙起穿衣，来拿夫手曰：“你嫁我，我不在你家！”佃户曰：“这花娘也要打死！”三人滚作一团，也不能打得。佃母适携肉、鸡从外归，问曰：“何为？”佃曰：“主人奸我妻，我在床上拿住，我要打死这两个。”母指主人曰：“你好人家子孙也，不该干此事。不如讨银与我媳赔丑罢。”主人曰：“便对三年苗与你。”佃取妇脚带，系住主颈曰：“我不肯。”出外取刀磨曰：“定杀死他！”母出外抢刀，曰：“他是官家舍，白的是银，黄的是金，要得他几多。若杀死他，我你也不得安生。”再入劝主曰：“我儿性子不好，你再写田契与他。”主人曰：“亦可。”佃母取纸与写契。佃户立旁，勒要更写毗连田，共凑二十铺，作价二十两。主人亦写与之。佃母再与子商曰：“本意只抵赖苗，不意多得二十两。今晚你须避开，再令媳妇陪他一宵，方服得他心，可保无事。”佃曰：“已得娶妻之本，就让他一宵。”
paragraphs.en: Next day after the meal, the tenant pretended to go to his father-in-law’s to borrow silver to pay the rent. The mother also told the daughter-in-law: “When the landlord comes there’s no dish; I’ll go to the upper village for a jin of meat, then to uncle’s for a chicken. Whether the rent can be paid or not, we should make a feast for the landlord. You prepare a brazier for him to warm himself.” The landlord outside already heard. After the two left, the wife brought out the brazier and fanned the fire. The landlord asked: “Where did your mama go?” The wife said: “To get dishes.” He asked again: “Where’s your husband?” The wife said: “To my mother’s to borrow silver to pay your rent; I don’t know if he’ll get it.” The landlord said: “No need to borrow from your mother; just borrow from you.” The wife said: “If I had silver I’d have sent it long ago.” The landlord said: “Sleep with me last night—or rather, if you’d slept with me, I’d write off the rent.” The wife said: “If sleeping can count as silver, come tonight and I’ll keep you company.” The landlord stood: “Don’t wait for night; luckily today’s no one, let’s play now. If your husband borrows silver, I’ll secretly weigh three qian for you to buy cloth; if there’s no silver, I’ll extend you to next year.” The woman agreed; they went into the room. The tenant, watching from a hidden place, quietly came out and waited outside the door. Hearing the two talking happily inside, he was naturally burning, and wished he could burst in. After a long while, the landlord said: “Get up.” The wife said: “No hurry.” Knowing it was done, he shouted outside: “Who are you talking with?” and burst in. The two were too hurried to hide. The tenant shouted: “Ai! You thief, you’ve raped my wife!” and dragged him off the bed to beat him. The wife hurriedly dressed, grabbed her husband’s hands: “You married me; I won’t stay in your house!” The tenant said: “This flower-girl should be beaten to death too!” The three rolled in a heap; he couldn’t really beat them. The mother just then came back with meat and chicken: “What’s this?” The tenant said: “The landlord raped my wife; I caught them on the bed; I’ll beat these two to death.” The mother pointed at the landlord: “You’re a son of a good family; you shouldn’t do this. Better pay silver to my daughter-in-law to make up for the shame.” The landlord said: “I’ll write off three years of seedling-rent.” The tenant took the wife’s foot-binding, tied the landlord’s neck: “I won’t agree.” He went out, took a knife, and sharpened it: “I’ll kill him for sure!” The mother rushed out, snatched the knife: “He’s from an official family; white is silver, yellow is gold—you can get plenty from him. If you kill him, you and I won’t live in peace either.” She went back in and urged the landlord: “My son’s temper is bad; write him a land deed too.” The landlord said: “All right.” The mother fetched paper for him to write a deed. The tenant stood by and forced him to also write the adjoining fields, totaling twenty pu, priced at twenty taels. The landlord wrote that too. The mother conferred with her son again: “We only meant to write off the rent; unexpectedly we got twenty taels extra. Tonight you should stay away, let the daughter-in-law keep him company one night, so his heart submits and we can keep things safe.” The tenant said: “I’ve already got back the capital of marrying a wife; I’ll yield him one night.”

paragraphs.zh: 半午后，方整酒出。佃欲请人陪，佃母曰：“不可，只我老人自陪。”三人同坐，主人只索饭吃回去。佃母曰：“适间儿子蠢性，千万勿怪，我自陪你。”叫儿子先吃饭，往母舅家，故说借银，相添买田。儿去讫，佃母呼妇出陪。主人曰：“你母子妆套弄我，明日必告官理论。”佃母发誓曰：“我若套弄你，我即死在今日！”佃妇泣曰：“若告我便缢死。”主人见妇泣，翻料其非套，曰：“我不管你有套否，今晚更与我睡一夜，便当送你。”佃母连声应曰：“凭媳妇。”妇曰：“拼定陪你。男人若有言，嫁我便是。”主人被此瞒过，只宿一宵而去，安然无后话。
paragraphs.en: After mid-morning they finally set out wine. The tenant wanted to invite people to sit with them. The mother said: “No; only I, an old person, will sit with him.” The three sat; the landlord only wanted rice so he could go home. The mother said: “Just now my son was stupid-tempered; please don’t take offense; I’ll keep you company.” She told her son to eat first and go to maternal uncle’s, pretending to borrow silver to help buy land. The son left. The mother called the wife out to sit. The landlord said: “You mother and son set a trap for me; tomorrow I’ll sue at the yamen.” The mother swore: “If I set a trap for you, may I die today!” The wife wept: “If you sue I’ll hang myself.” The landlord saw her weep, flipped to thinking it wasn’t a trap: “I don’t care if you had a trap or not; sleep with me one more night tonight and I’ll let you off.” The mother quickly said: “Up to the daughter-in-law.” The wife said: “I’ll definitely keep you company. If my man says a word, just marry me.” The landlord was fooled by this, stayed only one night and left; there was no later trouble.

paragraphs.zh: 按：佃母极狡猾，安排圈子已定，又令奸须过手，又令再陪一夜，方得主人心凉。不然，主佃之分，岂空套可笼？此佃母一狡棍也，述与后人知防。
paragraphs.en: Note: The tenant’s mother was extremely cunning: the trap was already set, she also required the act to be finished, then required another night of company, so the landlord’s heart would cool. Otherwise, given the landlord-tenant distinction, could an empty trap hold him? This tenant’s mother was a cunning swindler; I tell it so later people know to guard against it.

paragraphs.zh: 荆南道上，人多畜马，以租行客，日收其利。有三妇轻身同行，遇马夫牵回马三匹，三妇各租乘一匹。末婶曰：“伯母善乘马者先行，我二人不善乘者随后。”行不十里，末婶叫马夫扶下马小宜。马夫紧抱以下，有讨趣之意。末婶曰：“你讨我便宜。”马夫曰：“不敢！要紧挟些，方不跌。”末婶曰：“看你亦知趣。我久无丈夫的，亦不怕你挟。”马夫曰：“既不怕，前有小茅房，再同我相抱一抱何如？”妇曰：“要赶路。今晚在你家借歇，何如？”马夫曰：“无三铺床。”妇曰：“伯母两人同榻，我只傍床。”马夫曰：“你要傍我床，我不索你租马银。”妇人曰：“人比马价，你又讨便宜。”马夫曰：“两有便宜事，可不好干。”
paragraphs.en: On the Jingnan roads, people often keep horses to rent to travelers, collecting daily profit. Three women traveling light met a horse-handler leading back three horses; each woman rented one. The youngest said: “Auntie who rides well, go first; we two who don’t ride well will follow.” Before ten li, the youngest called the handler to help her down to relieve herself. He held her tightly to lower her, with a hint of taking advantage. The youngest said: “You’re taking liberties.” The handler said: “I wouldn’t dare! I have to hold a bit tight or you’ll fall.” The youngest said: “I see you know how to play. I’ve long had no husband; I’m not afraid of your holding.” The handler said: “If you’re not afraid, there’s a little thatched hut ahead; how about another hug?” The woman said: “We have to hurry. Tonight we’ll lodge at your house—how about that?” The handler said: “I haven’t three beds.” The woman said: “The two aunts can share a couch; I’ll just stay by your bed.” The handler said: “If you’ll stay by my bed, I won’t charge you horse rent.” The woman said: “A person compared with a horse’s price—you’re taking advantage again.” The handler said: “When both sides get something, isn’t it good to do?”

paragraphs.zh: 两人正在此私约，前面次伯母坠马。妇指马夫曰：“快去扶我小姆。”马夫行且回顾曰：“不要哄我。”妇曰：“小姆若跌坏，怕她不在半路歇？我你事一定成矣。”马夫忙奔前去。
paragraphs.en: While they were privately arranging this, the middle aunt ahead fell off her horse. The woman pointed: “Quick, go help my younger aunt.” The handler went, looking back: “Don’t trick me.” The woman said: “If the younger aunt is badly hurt, won’t she have to rest halfway? Then our business is sure to happen.” The handler hurried forward.

paragraphs.zh: 次母跌在路盘坐，挪脚曰：“跌伤了脚，又跌伤了腿。”马夫扶起上马，曰：“须赶路。”次姆曰：“我跌坏了，前去须买补损膏药贴，只好随路歇，赶不得梢头。你前去叫我大姆少待。”因挨延北两遭，前马去不止十餘里。马夫向前去追，后二妇跃马加鞭奔回。
paragraphs.en: The middle one sat on the road, rubbing her foot: “I hurt my foot, and my leg too.” The handler helped her on the horse: “We must hurry.” The middle one said: “I’m hurt; ahead we’ll have to buy bruise plaster; we can only rest along the way, can’t make the destination. You go ahead and tell my eldest aunt to wait a little.” By delaying twice like this, the front horse was more than ten li ahead. The handler went forward to catch up; the two women behind whipped their horses and raced back.

paragraphs.zh: 马夫前去赶不上，心忖曰：“任她前去，且在此等后二妇来，她自然要等齐同歇矣。”俟久不至，心又忖曰：“想必后路买膏药来。”因问行路人曰：“两妇人骑马的，到哪里了？”路人曰：“两妇人跑马如飞，此去不止二十里了。”马夫又问曰：“骑马是来此的，是去的？”路人曰：“是下去的。你快赶也来不及了。”马夫心无主意，慌忙走回原所，再问路人，皆云：“马去已远。”马夫追回十里，天已晚。再问行人，云：“不见妇人马矣。”三马从两路脱去，前后不能两追，马夫惟怅悒而归。
paragraphs.en: The handler couldn’t catch the one ahead, and thought: “Let her go on; I’ll wait here for the two behind; they’ll naturally wait to lodge together.” He waited long; they didn’t come. He thought again: “They must be buying plaster on the back road.” He asked a passerby: “The two women on horses—where have they gotten to?” The passerby said: “The two women are racing like flying; they’re more than twenty li that way.” The handler asked again: “Were they riding this way or going away?” The passerby said: “Going back down. Even if you hurry you won’t catch them.” The handler had no plan, hurried back to the original place, asked more people; all said: “The horses are already far.” He chased back ten li; it was already dark. Asked travelers again; they said they hadn’t seen the women or horses. The three horses had been taken off on two roads; he couldn’t chase both front and back. The handler could only go home dejected.

paragraphs.zh: 按：此巧脱处全在后妇小宜，与马夫私谈，以惑其心，以缠其时；次又中妇跌马，彼疑真不善骑者，又缠多时，则前马稳脱矣，故赚其前追，又安能及？后两妇奔回，彼唯疑跌伤来迟，岂料反奔而回乎？然亦马夫太痴：安有中途一遇，便许与你歇？马夫有何标致而妇恋之？其言太甘，其中必毒。故就其甜言处，便知是棍也。以妇人而有此高手，世道几何不鬼魅哉！
paragraphs.en: Note: The clever theft all hinged on the rear woman relieving herself, talking privately with the handler to confuse his mind and waste his time; then the middle woman falling, so he thought she truly couldn’t ride, wasting more time, so the front horse got away steadily. Thus they lured him to chase ahead—how could he catch up? The two behind raced back; he only thought the injured one was slow—how would he guess they were racing the other way? But the handler was too stupid: who, meeting on the road, would at once promise to lodge with you? What looks did the handler have that women would cling to him? Words too sweet have poison in them. From the sweet talk itself, you know it’s a swindle. When women have this level of skill, how can the world not be full of ghosts?

stories.title_en: A Nun Scatters Beads to Lure a Woman into Adultery

paragraphs.zh: 白鉴妻向氏，大有姿色。鉴专好酒，与妻不甚绸缪。为王军门公干，差之上京。妻向氏在家开纸马店，常遣婢兰香接钱交易。夫去日久，向氏时出店看人。有宁朝贤见之，爱其美，注目看之；向亦不避。朝贤归，与心友曹知高谋，欲诱此妇。曹曰：“若骗妇人，须用一女人在内行事，方易成就。古云‘山贼攻山贼，水寇擒水寇’。此中法华庵尼姑妙真，常往来各家，汝去托之，其事易矣。”朝贤闻教大喜，即寻法华庵来，见了妙真，以银二两送之，托其通纸马店内白鉴之妻；若事成之后，再有重谢。尼姑曰：“此也不难，你三日后来讨回音。”宁再三嘱之而去。
paragraphs.en: Bai Jian’s wife, née Xiang, was very attractive. Jian loved wine and was not very intimate with his wife. On business for Commander Wang, he was sent to the capital. Wife Xiang kept a paper-offering shop at home, and often sent the maid Lanxiang to take money and trade. The husband gone a long time, Xiang sometimes came out to the shop to watch people. Ning Chaoxian saw her, liked her looks, and stared; Xiang did not avoid it. Chaoxian went home and plotted with close friend Cao Zhigao to lure this woman. Cao said: “To trick a woman you need a woman working inside, then it’s easy. The old saying: ‘It takes a mountain bandit to attack mountain bandits; water pirates to catch water pirates.’ Nun Miaozhen of Fahua Convent often visits various houses; go ask her, and the matter will be easy.” Chaoxian was delighted, went to Fahua Convent, saw Miaozhen, gave her two taels, and asked her to make contact with Bai Jian’s wife in the paper-offering shop; if it succeeded, there would be further heavy thanks. The nun said: “Not hard; come in three days for a reply.” Ning charged her again and again and left.

paragraphs.zh: 尼姑将手中数珠剪断绳子，捻定在手，往白鉴店前转行几次，不见向氏，空回了。次日又往，见向氏在店坐。尼姑故将断绳珠撒放满地，多有滚在污泥去者，俯躬满地捡之。向氏见，叫之入，以水与洗，又净手讫。尼姑再三拜谢而去。
paragraphs.en: The nun cut the string of the beads in her hand, held them, walked back and forth in front of Bai Jian’s shop several times; didn’t see Xiang, and went back empty. The next day she went again, saw Xiang sitting in the shop. The nun deliberately scattered the broken-string beads all over the ground; many rolled into the mud; she bent to pick them up all over. Xiang saw, called her in, gave water to wash, and clean hands. The nun thanked again and again and left.

paragraphs.zh: 至明日，尼姑买糕、果、饼、面四品，叫人往向氏家谢。向氏喜，遣人请尼姑来吃素酒。席间，向氏问曰：“你几岁出家？”尼姑曰：“我半路出家。”向曰：“因何事出家？”尼曰：“因嫁个人，好赌钱饮酒，终日在外，有夫与无夫同，故誓愿出家。”向氏叹气一声道：“招这人不如勿嫁。”尼见他动心，又问曰：“娘子如何叹气？”赂曰：“我病亦似你。今嫁个人，只好饮酒，从来不要妻子，一年不欢会几次。今又奉差远去，似无夫一般。”尼知此妇有春怨，即乘机曰：“男人心歹者多。唯我庵前宁朝贤，当日爱妻如命，只其妻没福而死。今央我择再娶，谁妇人遇此者，真日日得欢喜也。”向氏听了，口中不语。尼亦不好再调，酒完而去。
paragraphs.en: The next day the nun bought four items—cakes, fruit, pastry, noodles—and sent someone to Xiang’s to thank her. Xiang was pleased, and sent someone to invite the nun for a vegetarian drink. At the table Xiang asked: “How old were you when you left home?” The nun said: “I left home halfway through life.” Xiang asked: “Why?” The nun said: “I married a man who loved gambling and drinking, always out; having a husband was like having none, so I vowed to leave home.” Xiang sighed: “Better not marry than marry such a man.” The nun saw she was moved, and asked: “Why does Madam sigh?” Xiang said: “My illness is like yours. I married a man who only likes drinking, never wants a wife; in a year we don’t happily meet a few times. Now he’s been sent far away; it’s like having no husband.” The nun knew this woman had spring resentment, and seized the chance: “Many men’s hearts are bad. Only Ning Chaoxian in front of my convent loved his wife like his life; only she had no luck and died. Now he asks me to choose a remarriage; any woman who meets him would truly be happy every day.” Xiang heard and said nothing. The nun did not dare tease further; after wine she left.

paragraphs.zh: 第三日，朝贤整饰衣冠，来庵问回音，妙真曰：“事有九分成了。凡妇人与夫和顺者，极难挑动。昨向氏请我，知她心中恨夫；又别夫日久，但有机会，便可到手。今须讨银与我，办一盛席，请来用好酒灌醉，必在我床睡，你便解开衣，慢慢行事，恣你所为矣。但醒来之时，须备镯甸簪珥类送之，可买其心，方可长久相交。”宁听了拜下：“若如此，死生不忘。今再送银五两，你速作席请来。”
paragraphs.en: On the third day Chaoxian dressed up and came to the convent for a reply. Miaozhen said: “Nine-tenths done. Women who get along with their husbands are very hard to move. Yesterday Xiang invited me; I learned she resents her husband; and she’s been apart a long time; given a chance, she’s within reach. Now I need silver; I’ll prepare a rich feast, invite her, pour good wine till she’s drunk; she’ll sleep in my bed; you undo her clothes and slowly proceed, do as you like. But when she wakes, have bracelets, hairpins and such ready to give her, to buy her heart, so you can have a long affair.” Ning bowed: “If so, I won’t forget in life or death. Here’s five more taels; quickly make the feast and invite her.”

paragraphs.zh: 妙真遣人买好肴好酒，叫厨子整治丰洁，先遣人去请，后自到家邀行。向氏欢喜，同兰香打轿而来。见酒席十分美盛，曰：“你还请何人？”妙真曰：“专请娘子，并无别客。”向氏曰：“一人亦不消如此破费，怎吃得许多？”妙真曰：“我无亲骨肉，多感娘子知己，愿结为姊妹，当个知心人。”向氏笑曰：“我和你知心，不能相爬痒痛。”饮了几杯，问曰：“此酒香而甜，其价必贵。”尼曰：“是前日宁大官送的，亦不识其价。”又劝饮。向氏曰：“酒甜吃得下，只恐易醉。”尼曰：“若醉暂在我房少睡，醒后回去不迟。不知娘子尊量，饮几许方醉。”向氏曰：“夜间恐睡不着，常可饮一瓶。若不饮酒，如何得睡？”尼曰：“若自家人在家，只吃他一杯，便可睡矣。”向氏曰：“我和你说知心话，虽醉只半夜便醒。丈夫在家，只是贪酒，再不要干事。我醒来极是难熬，哪止得我渴想？”妙真曰：“似此有老公的，与我无有的一般。我日间犹过了，只夜来过不得，惟怨前生未修种也。”向曰：“的是如此。今日须极醉，求一夜可忘却。”少顷醉倒，遣兰香先回看家，旋在尼床少睡。
paragraphs.en: Miaozhen sent people to buy good food and wine, had a cook prepare it richly and cleanly, first sent someone to invite, then went herself to fetch her. Xiang was glad, and came with Lanxiang by sedan. Seeing the feast so lavish, she said: “Who else did you invite?” Miaozhen said: “Only Madam; no other guest.” Xiang said: “For one person you needn’t spend so much; how can we eat so much?” Miaozhen said: “I have no blood kin; I’m grateful Madam is a kindred spirit; I want to become sisters, a true confidante.” Xiang laughed: “You and I are confidantes, but we can’t scratch each other’s itches.” After a few cups she asked: “This wine is fragrant and sweet; it must be expensive.” The nun said: “Official Ning sent it the other day; I don’t know the price.” She urged more drink. Xiang said: “It’s sweet and goes down, but I fear I’ll get drunk easily.” The nun said: “If drunk, sleep a while in my room; go home after you wake, no rush. I don’t know Madam’s capacity—how much before you’re drunk?” Xiang said: “At night if I can’t sleep, I can often drink a bottle. If I don’t drink, how can I sleep?” The nun said: “If one’s own man is at home, one cup from him and you can sleep.” Xiang said: “I’ll tell you a confidante’s truth: even drunk I wake by midnight. Husband at home only greedily drinks, never wants to do the deed. When I wake it’s hard to bear—how can it stop my thirst?” Miaozhen said: “So having a husband is the same as my having none. Daytime I can still get through; only nights I can’t; I only resent I didn’t plant merit in a past life.” Xiang said: “Exactly so. Today I must get very drunk, hoping for one night of forgetting.” Shortly she collapsed drunk. They sent Lanxiang home first to watch the house; Xiang then slept a while on the nun’s bed.

paragraphs.zh: 朝贤向氏睡，即来解其衣带，如死去而暖的一样，凭他恣意恋战，其味甚美。少歇又一次，亦不醒。朝贤双手搂定妇人睡，直到半夜醒来，衣已脱去。觉有男子在身边，又觉腰间爽快，浑身通泰，低声问道：“你是何人？”朝贤道：“心肝，我想你几时，今日方才得偷两次，还要明日和我一好。”向氏曰：“你谋既就，切不可与外人知。”朝贤曰：“只尼姑知道，除外何人得知？”
paragraphs.en: While Xiang was asleep, Chaoxian came and undid her clothes and sash. She was like one dead yet warm; he did as he pleased, and the flavor was very fine. After a rest, once more; still she did not wake. Chaoxian slept holding her with both arms until midnight. She woke; her clothes were already off. She felt a man beside her, and a pleasant ease at her waist, her whole body comfortable. Softly she asked: “Who are you?” Chaoxian said: “Darling, how long I’ve wanted you; today I finally stole two times; tomorrow you must be good with me too.” Xiang said: “Your plot has succeeded; just don’t let outsiders know.” Chaoxian said: “Only the nun knows; who else would know?”

paragraphs.zh: 又睡到天微明，向氏起。朝贤以镯甸与之，又抱亲嘴。两人兴浓，再战一次，携手出门。妙真已在候，忍笑不住，曰：“好酒也！”向氏曰：“好计也！”朝贤曰：“好姻缘也！”妙真曰：“既有此好，何以谢我？”紧抱贤曰：“亏我脚酸也，要和我好为谢。”贤曰：“力尽耳，今夜不忘谢。”向氏曰：“从今夜夜都让谢你。”朝贤曰：“后会可长，谢亦可长。”从此常与向氏往来，皆由尼姑此番之引诱也。
paragraphs.en: They slept till faint dawn; Xiang rose. Chaoxian gave her bracelets, and kissed her. Both still eager, they did it once more, and went out hand in hand. Miaozhen was already waiting, and could not hold her laugh: “Good wine!” Xiang said: “Good scheme!” Chaoxian said: “Good match!” Miaozhen said: “Since it’s this good, how will you thank me?” She tightly hugged Chaoxian: “My legs ache from the work; be good with me as thanks.” Chaoxian said: “I’m spent; tonight I won’t forget to thank you.” Xiang said: “From tonight every night we’ll yield the thanks to you.” Chaoxian said: “Meetings can last; thanks can last too.” From then on he often visited Xiang, all from this lure by the nun.

paragraphs.zh: 按：妇人虽贞，倘遇淫妇引之，无不入于邪者。凡妇之谨身，唯知耻耳，唯畏人知耳。苟一失身之后，耻心既丧，又何所不为？故人家唯慎尼姑、媒婆等，勿使往来，亦防微杜渐之正道也。
paragraphs.en: Note: Even a chaste woman, if led by a wanton woman, will enter into evil. A woman’s guarding her person is only knowing shame, only fearing people will know. Once she’s lost herself, shame is gone—what won’t she do? So households should be careful with nuns, matchmakers, and the like; don’t let them come and go. This is the right way to stop trouble at the start.
